title: Roston Chase: Reading an All-Round Cricket Record
excerpt: Read Roston Chase’s batting and bowling records with format, role and sample size in mind, using the official West Indies player profile.
body:
Roston Chase's official West Indies profile contains separate batting, bowling and fielding statistics. Those categories describe different contributions and should not be collapsed into a vague all-round label. Start by choosing the format and period, then ask what role the team needed in that set of matches.

## Batting average is not the whole innings

Average depends on runs and dismissals, including how not-outs are treated. Strike rate measures scoring speed. A lower-order contribution during a rescue effort should be read differently from an innings built on a strong platform. Entry score, remaining partners and pitch conditions help explain the difference.

Use completed scorecards for individual examples. A current career figure can change after the next match, so write down the date when comparing profiles. Do not mix a domestic competition with an international format without saying so.

## Bowling contribution can be flexible

An all-rounder's bowling allocation depends on team balance and the match situation. A captain may use spin to control scoring, attack a particular batter or manage specialist bowlers' workloads. The purpose is not always obvious from wickets alone.

Read overs, runs conceded and economy rate alongside dismissals. Note whether the spell occurred in a long innings or a short chase. A small sample can produce a dramatic average that is not representative of the wider record.

## Fielding belongs in the analysis

Catches are recorded, but many saved runs and pressure-building movements are not captured by a simple total. Describe visible contributions carefully and avoid inventing a numerical value for an unmeasured action. A highlight compilation naturally favours spectacular moments over consistent positioning.

## Make a balanced player note

Choose three matches in one format. Summarise the batting task, bowling task and outcome for each. Then explain what changed between those situations. This produces a more useful assessment than deciding a player's value from one match-winning clip or one poor outing. Our [cricket scorecard guide](/blogs/new-zealand-vs-india-4th-t20i-october-30-2026-guide/) explains the supporting calculations. The historical skyline is a cricket-event illustration and not a photograph of Chase.
